authenticity.evidence: Around 10 PROM clones were deployed within minutes of each other (pairs created 1790252269-1790254257), and seven share the same image. This one was created and migrated in the same second on a Meteora virtual curve, which points to a scripted launch. GMGN flags 32 bundler wallets. Recent flow looks like bot churn: in the last 5 minutes there were 545 buys and 532 sells from only 39 buyers and 37 sellers, and over the hour there were 81 unique sellers against 2089 buyers, which suggests airdrop or dust-style buyer counts. There is no DexScreener profile, and GMGN shows only 5 page visits.
authenticity.uncertainty: There is no X data, so I can't check whether the usePromX status post is real or an impersonation. The 2089 unique buyers could include some real retail, but the number of real participants is probably far smaller.

structured_output.counterargument: If the usePromX post is a real announcement of an official PromX token and this contract turns out to be the one it links to, attention could concentrate here and a re-rate from about $108k to above $220k would be easy. The creator has had a token reach a $2.1M ATH. Mint and freeze authority are renounced, GMGN reports lp_burn_ratio 1.0, and there are no taxes.

structural_risks: RugCheck flags LP as largely unlocked (0% locked in one market), which conflicts with GMGN's lp_burn_ratio of 1.0
One unlabeled address holds 80.05%, probably a pool vault but not confirmed; GeckoTerminal shows the top 10 holding 98%
Only about $24k of liquidity against $550k of hourly volume, a wash-trading profile
Volume is split across roughly 10 same-ticker clones

narrative.description: The ticker PROM/PromX seems tied to an X post (usePromX status link). Many deployers are racing to launch copies, and there is also an established $67M PROM token.
narrative.why_spreading: Clone deployers and volume bots jump on any ticker that trends from an X post. Nothing shows organic interest in this particular contract.

source_coverage.notes: No internet in this condition. I used only the packet.

structured_output.thesis: This is one of about 10 PROM clones launched within minutes of each other. It is neither the leader nor canonical. Its volume looks bot-driven, and price has been falling for the last 30 minutes. It has thin liquidity, bundlers, and conflicting LP-lock signals. Doubling before a 50% drop or a dead pair is unlikely.

token_connection.why_this_token: The name matches the usePromX link. The GMGN website field (promx.fun) is shared by an unknown number of clones, and nothing marks this contract as the official one.
token_connection.competing_tokens: There are about 7 same-minute PROM clones, several larger than this one: EFW3 at $249k, 8xhS at $224k with $4.1M/h volume, UWiW at $253k, and 7MsR at $292k. There is also the established Prom (FkeG) at $67M.

unknowns: Whether the usePromX post is real and which contract, if any, it endorses
Whether LP is actually burned (GMGN) or unlocked (RugCheck)
How much of the 2089 buyers are real
structured_output.what_is_happening: PROM is a pumpswap pair, about 37 minutes old, that migrated instantly from a Meteora virtual curve. It rose 124% in its first hour to about $108k mcap on $550k of volume. Over the last 30 minutes it has drifted down 5-6% while bots trade back and forth in balanced flow. Many PROM clones launched at the same time, and several of them are larger.
